_comment: SDR fleet policy revision 4.1 (SB7, 2026-07-08) — SINGLE-HOST on the M1 Mac mini (host confirmed by Will; Intel mini = cold spare). Source of truth for device->role allocation, RSPduo modes, USB grouping, and tuner-broker invariants. The broker, config generators, and wiring card all read THIS file. Address devices by serial ONLY; USB position is never trusted. NOTE: top-level `version` is the POLICY SCHEMA version the broker enforces (broker/policy.py SUPPORTED_POLICY_VERSIONS = (2,)) — it stays 2. The human arrangement label lives in `revision`. HARDWARE CHANGE 2026-07-08: Will physically REMOVED the RSPduo serial 180903EF32 (the former RSP-A / digital device) to use on a DIFFERENT computer — it is gone from the mini (see retired_devices, status relocated). The ONE RSP remaining on the mini is serial 1809063632 (the former RSP-B, previously retired), which now carries DIGITAL. Arrangement is otherwise unchanged (option C): the one RSP runs digital via SDRTrunk native API (dual-tuner, up to 2 P25 systems); both analog bands run on RTLs; airband/ground/sounding unchanged. See docs/sb7-northstar-program.md §4.
_hardware_change_4_1: RSP-A (180903EF32) was physically unplugged and taken to another host. Digital therefore moves to the only RSP still attached: serial 1809063632 (ex-RSP-B). CONFIRM ON THE BOX which RSP is present (see _detection below) before trusting this — the policy EXPECTS 1809063632 but the physical truth must be verified. The proven-clean digital-on-RSP result was measured on 180903EF32 specifically; digital on 1809063632 is therefore marked status=pending-soak until it is confirmed clean on this serial.
_detection: On the mini, enumerate connected SDRplay devices and read the serial: `SoapySDRUtil --find="driver=sdrplay"` (lists each RSP with its serial), or the project's own check `bash macos/install/post-install-checks.sh` (verifies apiService + RSPduo-on-USB), or in SDRTrunk: View -> Tuners. Expected serial: 1809063632. If a DIFFERENT serial shows up, update this policy to match the physical device.
_rationale_single_rsp: Running TWO SDRplay RSPs on one host is toxic: both funnel through the single sdrplay_apiService, and concurrent opens across two physical RSPs produce the 0x6bed segfault + corrupt IQ. With 180903EF32 removed, exactly ONE RSP (1809063632) remains — which is the safe state by construction. It is opened by exactly ONE process (SDRTrunk, native API), so there is no cross-process master/slave path and 0x6bed stays unreachable even at dual-tuner.
_rationale_arrangement_C: Digital on the RSP (native SDRplay API) is the only dual-tuner path this project has proven clean, and gives 2 P25 systems from one device. Analog on RTLs uses proven-clean configs: ground NFM on RTL 61108285 (the 2026-06-18 fix) and airband AM on the Blog V4 (what rtl_airband ran for years). Two pieces are pending-soak: airband AM on an RTL (new under the current chirp engine) and — new in revision 4.1 — digital on RSP serial 1809063632 (the proven result was on 180903EF32; reconfirm on this serial).

host.cold_spare: Mac mini 2018 Intel (16 GB, macOS Sequoia ceiling — security updates end ~fall 2027)

digital_capacity._primary: RSP (serial 1809063632) in SDRTrunk native Dual Tuner mode = 2 P25 systems at once, one per ~2 MHz tuner. MTRTRS ships first on tuner 1; the 2nd system slots onto tuner 2 (Will to name it) with no hardware change (SDRTrunk restart to add). Each monitored SITE must fit ~2 MHz — verify spans in SDRangel before committing.
digital_capacity._pending_soak: The 2-P25 native-dual-tuner capability was proven on the now-removed 180903EF32. Reconfirm it holds on 1809063632 before treating digital as validated (RSPduo units are the same model, so this is expected to pass — but it is a different physical device, so soak it).
digital_capacity.growth_to_3: A 3rd P25 system = add a 4TH RTL (not currently attached — only 3 RTLs on the M1) to the SAME SDRTrunk instance. All 3 attached RTLs are committed to analog + sounding, so a 3rd P25 system needs new hardware.

invariants._why_one_rsp: Two RSPs sharing the one sdrplay_apiService is the root cause of the 0x6bed segfault + IQ corruption. Exactly one RSP is permitted. With 180903EF32 removed, the one remaining RSP is 1809063632. The broker REFUSES any claim on a second RSP serial.
invariants._why: The single permitted RSP (1809063632) runs dual-tuner via SDRTrunk's native API in ONE process. There is no second dual-tuner device, so 0x6bed stays unreachable. chirp never opens the RSP (analog is RTL-only), so the Soapy cross-process master/slave corruption path is also out of the picture.
invariants._why_gap: The apiService does not safely serialize concurrent sdrplay_api_Open calls; grants on kind=rspduo are spaced by this gap.

rspduo_daemon._note: One apiService for the ONE RSP (serial 1809063632), opened ONLY by SDRTrunk via the native SDRplay API for digital P25. chirp does NOT open the RSP (analog is RTL-only). SDRTrunk launches once and stays up (KeepAlive). It claims serial 1809063632 through the tuner-broker so nothing else can open the device.

devices.label: RSP-DIGITAL

tuners._note: D3 launch target. Pin the MTRTRS control channel to this tuner via SDRTrunk's per-channel Preferred Tuner.
2nd P25 system — Will names it. Slots on here with no hardware change; SDRTrunk restart to add. Verify its site span fits ~2 MHz.

devices._note: The ONE RSP now on the host: serial 1809063632, the former RSP-B (was chirp-airband ST under v2.1, then retired, now DIGITAL after 180903EF32 was removed 2026-07-08). DIGITAL ONLY, SDRTrunk native Dual Tuner (NOT osmosdr/Soapy). No device_args; SDRTrunk manages both tuners internally from its playlist. The broker leases the ONE serial 1809063632 to SDRTrunk (dual_tuner=true consumes the single allowed dual slot). STATUS pending-soak: the proven-clean digital-on-RSP result was on 180903EF32 (now gone) — reconfirm on 1809063632 (same RSPduo model, expected to pass). CONFIRM this is the serial physically present (see _detection).

devices.label: AIRBAND
devices.reliability: best-RF-quality (R828D tuner + TCXO); historically flaky USB re-enumeration on micro (error -71) — watch during soak on the M1's own ports/cables
devices._note: AIRBAND AM via chirp on the Blog V4 RTL (gr-osmosdr 'rtl=' backend, exactly like ground). The RSP is digital-only, so chirp never touches it. STATUS pending-soak: airband-AM-on-RTL is proven by lineage (rtl_airband ran Nashville airband AM on RTLs for years) and by composition (chirp-on-RTL proven on ground; chirp AM demod proven), but not yet soaked as a unit under the current chirp engine. Unchanged by the 2026-07-08 RSP removal. No bandwidth_hz needed for RTL (0 = driver default). LO scheduler hops the airband list within the RTL's ~2.4 MHz window.

devices.serial_status: PRESENT-on-M1 2026-07-05 (was micro's WX dongle; micro-confirmed stable)
devices.label: GROUND
devices._note: FIXED, 24/7 core analog. Ground NFM on this RTL is the proven 2026-06-18 fix. Gain 30-35 (40 clips the front end). Unchanged across revisions. gr-osmosdr addresses it by the native 'rtl=61108285' source type. Unaffected by the RSP removal.

devices.serial_status: PRESENT-on-M1 2026-07-05 (NESDR SMArt v5; new to the fleet, reliability TBD in soak)
devices.label: SOUNDING
devices._note: "Sounding" = the atmospheric-sounding decoder family: ACARS + VDL2 (~130-137 MHz) and radiosonde (~400-406 MHz, time-shared). Dedicated, unshared. Unchanged across revisions. None of the sounding decoders are broker-integrated yet. Waterfall (/sb5 Live IQ) remains DEFERRED. Unaffected by the RSP removal.

retired_devices._note: REMOVED / RELOCATED 2026-07-08 — Will physically UNPLUGGED this RSPduo and took it to a DIFFERENT computer. It is no longer attached to the mini. Digital moved to the remaining RSP (1809063632, the former RSP-B, now active in devices[]). This is a physical relocation, not a fleet retirement for cause: the device is fine, it's just elsewhere now. If it ever returns to the mini, remember the one-RSP invariant — you cannot run it alongside 1809063632 (two RSPs on one host is toxic); it would have to REPLACE the other, not join it.

G2._note: RSP (1809063632, digital, dual-tuner) direct-cabled, own controller, no hub. (Was RSP-B's port; RSP-A's G1 port is now empty after the relocation.)

G3._note: 3 RTLs on a powered hub: AIRBAND (Blog V4), GROUND, SOUNDING. VERIFY controller grouping on the box with `system_profiler SPUSBDataType`; consider a 2nd powered hub if throughput/overflow shows up in soak (three 2.4 Msps RTL streams).

broker._lock_key_note: One consumer per physical serial. The RSP (1809063632) has exactly one consumer (SDRTrunk, which owns both its tuners internally via the native API), and each of the three RTLs has exactly one consumer. No tuner-granular arbitration needed.
